title: God, The Forgiving Lord, Is Kind To
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: Comparison is carried here from god, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor toward nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.
whyItMatters: This shabad is useful when life feels envious, unsettled, small, because it keeps comparison inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private mood.
takeaway: Comparison steadies when nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.

lines.translation: God, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor.
He loves His devotees, and He is always merciful to them.
The Patron of the patronless, the Lord of the Universe, the Sustainer of the world,
The Primal Being, the Creator of the Creation.
The Support of the breath of life of His devotees.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਜੋ ਜਪੈ ਸੁ ਹੋਇ ਪੁਨੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo jo japai su hoi puneet ||
lines.translation: Whoever meditates on Him is sanctified,
focusing the mind in loving devotional worship.
I am unworthy, lowly and ignorant.
Nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God. ||7||

structure: The opening movement names the pressure directly: god, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor.
The middle movement deepens the correction by holding the mind inside the Support of the breath of life of His devotees.
The closing movement leaves a return you can actually keep: nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.
